project.name: Doshomik
project.title: Doshomik backend guide
project.lede: How the API in apps/api is put together: every endpoint, what it checks, what it reads and writes, and what happens after it returns. Generated from the running route table and the source code.

groups.name: Outside /v1
groups.desc: Health check, the storage and CDN stand-ins, and share-link fallbacks.

groups.name: App API
groups.desc: What the Android app calls. Everything except sign-in needs a signed-in user.

groups.name: Admin API
groups.desc: The admin panel. Staff role plus two-factor sign-in.

access.name: Public
access.desc: No sign-in. Sign-in routes are rate limited per IP.

access.name: Signed link
access.desc: The token in the path is the permission (HMAC, short-lived).

access.name: Signed in
access.desc: authenticate: a valid access token, a live session and an active account.

access.name: Moderator
access.desc: requireRole('moderator'): moderator or admin, with two-factor sign-in.

front.name: Fastify front door
front.text: Every request gets a server-made UUID request id (client ids are ignored), CORS, compression and ETags. onSend adds x-request-id and x-content-type-options: nosniff, plus HSTS in production. Signed tokens in /storage/raw and /media/s paths are redacted from the logs.

auth.name: authenticate
auth.text: Verifies the HS256 access token (15 minutes), then one indexed query checks the session is not revoked or expired and the account is active, so signing out or suspension takes effect at once. Sets request.auth = { userId, role, sessionId, mfaEnabled }. With DEV_AUTH_BYPASS a request with no Authorization header acts as DEV_AUTH_USER, or the username in x-dev-user.

role.name: requireRole
role.text: Staff routes: admins may do anything moderators can. Without two-factor sign-in the answer is 403 MFA_REQUIRED.

limit.name: Rate limit
limit.text: @fastify/rate-limit, opted into per route, checked in preHandler so per-user limits know the user. Counters are in memory per process until Redis exists. Over the limit: 429. Off in tests.

validate.name: zod validation
validate.text: fastify-type-provider-zod parses params, query string and body before the handler runs. A failure is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR with one entry per problem in details. Ids are UUIDs (publicId); topics and fields use slugs.

handler.name: Route handler
handler.text: Routes do HTTP only: they take the parsed input, call a service with internal ids and map the rows to the public shape (public UUIDs, never internal ids).

service.name: Services
service.text: Services own the SQL and the rules. They take a Db (the pool or a transaction). Queries that return user or team content build their WHERE clause from db/visibility.ts: blocks both ways, private accounts, drafts, deleted rows.

db.name: PostgreSQL
db.text: Kysely over pg with a statement timeout. A write that needs follow-up work inserts its outbox event in the same transaction, so the event exists exactly when the change committed.

response.name: Response
response.text: JSON with public ids. Lists are { items, next_cursor } with an encrypted keyset cursor. Errors are always { error: { code, message, request_id, details? } }, never a stack trace. Something you may not see is 404, not 403.

outbox.name: Outbox → worker
outbox.text: After the response, the worker (a separate process) claims the event and does its database work in one transaction: counters ±1, notification rows. Push and email run after that commit, best effort. A failing event is retried, up to 10 attempts.

facts: A separate process: pnpm worker. The API never waits on it.
One worker at a time: it takes a Postgres advisory lock at start-up and a second copy exits.
Each loop repeats its work at once while there is work, and sleeps its idle interval when there is none.
A loop error is logged and the loop carries on. SIGINT or SIGTERM lets the current work finish first.

loops.media: Processes the oldest upload in status processing: ffprobe and sharp checks, metadata stripped, WebP variants or an HLS ladder and poster, then status ready and a media.ready event. Its own loop so a long transcode never delays notifications.
loops.outbox: Up to 50 pending events per batch, each claimed and handled in one transaction. Push and email are sent after commit.
loops.papers: Paper ingestion for the Research tab: up to 10 due papers from OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar, Hugging Face trending every 6 hours, then the trend rank. Off with PAPER_SYNC_ENABLED=false.
loops.maintenance: Hourly: purge deleted accounts and posts after 30 days, recount stored counters, re-rank the collection, delete abandoned uploads, old sessions, used codes and old events.

conventions.name: Versioned
conventions.text: Everything the app calls is under /v1. Installed app versions stay around for months; GET /v1/app/config can require an update.

conventions.name: Public ids only
conventions.text: Requests and responses use UUIDs (public_id) or slugs. Internal numeric ids never leave the server, not even inside access tokens.

conventions.name: Pagination
conventions.text: Lists return { items, next_cursor }. Keyset pagination on (created_at, id), or on rank, with an AES-GCM encrypted cursor. A tampered cursor is 400 INVALID_CURSOR.

conventions.name: 404, not 403
conventions.text: Something the caller may not see (a private account's post, a draft, a blocked user) answers 404, so its existence is not revealed.

conventions.name: One error shape
conventions.text: { error: { code, message, request_id, details? } }. The code is stable; the client branches on it. request_id finds the full error in the logs.

conventions.name: Toggle writes
conventions.text: Likes, saves, follows and similar are PUT to turn on and DELETE to turn off, both idempotent, answering 204.

conventions.name: Side effects through the outbox
conventions.text: Counters, notifications, push and email are never done in the request. The request writes an outbox event in its transaction; the worker does the rest.

conventions.name: Audit
conventions.text: Every admin action writes an audit_log row in the same transaction (lib/audit.ts).
